μ(z) = k(z)⊤(K + vI)−1y

a) What happens to G if f = μ? (Medeiros et al. 2025)
b) How high does G get across functions f ~ GP(μ, S)?
G(t+1) = f(z(t)), trained on 1978–2019. In b), each of 500 functions f is summarised by the high monthly values of its run (95th percentile of the last 100 months): median and 95 % interval.
G: large green algae; t: month; z: last four values of G, phosphate, two temperatures; GP: Gaussian process; μ: posterior mean; S: posterior covariance; C: prior covariance; k(z): similarity of z to the training months; K: similarities among them; v: noise variance; I: identity matrix; y: observed next-month values
